topic: Using Declarations in Derived Classes to Inherit Constructors
explanation: In modern C++, derived classes can inherit constructors from their base classes using 'using' declarations. This feature simplifies code by allowing the derived class to automatically acquire the base class constructors, enabling object creation with the same parameter sets without explicitly redefining them. It enhances code reuse and maintains consistency, especially when dealing with complex inheritance hierarchies.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how the derived class 'D2' inherits constructors from its base classes 'B1' and 'B2' using 'using' declarations. When creating 'obj1' with no arguments, the default constructors of 'B1' and 'B2' are invoked. When creating 'obj2' with an integer argument, the 'D2' constructor is called explicitly, but 'D2' can also inherit the parameterized constructors of 'B1' and 'B2' if needed. This showcases modern C++'s ability to simplify constructor inheritance and promote code reuse in inheritance hierarchies.
